messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 218 omitted, sha256 499c10259b0abb74>
</document>

<hypothesis>
All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 80
reason: Section 2 defines Confidential Information to include information disclosed in circumstances of confidence or that the parties would understand to be confidential, without requiring express identification by the Disclosing Party.
<quote check="exact">would be understood by the parties, exercising reasonable business judgment, to be confidential</quote>
<quote check="exact">is disclosed in circumstances of confidence</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 82
reason: Confidential Information includes information that is not designated or marked but is disclosed in confidence or would reasonably be understood as confidential, so express identification is not required for all of it.
<quote check="exact">is disclosed in circumstances of confidence, or would be understood by the parties, exercising reasonable business judgment, to be confidential</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 88
reason: Confidential Information also covers information that is not designated as confidential but is disclosed in circumstances of confidence or would reasonably be understood to be confidential, so express identification is not required.
<quote check="exact">is disclosed in circumstances of confidence, or would be understood by the parties, exercising reasonable business judgment, to be confidential</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 85, "quotes": ["is disclosed in circumstances of confidence, or would be understood by the parties, exercising reasonable business judgment, to be confidential"], "reason": "Section 2 covers information that is not designated as confidential but is disclosed in confidential circumstances or would reasonably be understood as confidential, so express identification is not required."}
